slides.texte_overlay:
how to own any room
you walk into
Pause at the door for two seconds. Look around the room before you walk in. That small stop makes you look calm and in control, instead of rushing in unnoticed.
Greet the host first, then the people you know. Thank the person who invited you before anything else. Good manners at the door set the tone for the whole evening.
Introduce people to each other. "Have you two met? You both just moved here." The man who connects others naturally becomes the centre of the room.
Hold your drink in your left hand. Your right hand stays free and dry for handshakes. It's a small detail, but it makes every greeting smooth and confident.
Move around, don't anchor yourself in one corner. Spend ten minutes with each group. Being seen across the whole room makes people feel you belong everywhere.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A head full of good stories lets you join any group with something worth saying.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. You'll join any group with something worth saying.

slides.texte_overlay: Leave while the energy is high. Say goodbye properly, thank the host, and go before the night fades. People remember the man who left them wanting more.
